title: Learn JAX.
Build working models.
hero.intro: From arrays and gradients to training, evaluation, and deployment. Learn the ideas, run the experiments, and build with an AI tutor alongside you.
hero.note: Start with basic Python and a laptop CPU. The course is in active development.
hero.author: Taha Bouhsine

tutor.title: Learn with your own AI tutor
tutor.hosts: Codex · Claude Code · Cursor · other skill-enabled agents
tutor.command: npx skills add . --skill start-learning learn-jax jax-course-guide check-jax
tutor.prompt: Use start-learning to help me learn JAX from this workspace.
tutor.description: Start with a placement check, choose a learning path, and work through explanations and exercises with your agent.

directions.title: Where do you want to take it?
directions.intro: Start with the same foundations. Then follow the work that interests you.

items.title: Training
items.description: Build training loops, neural networks and small Transformers.

items.title: Inference
items.description: Take a trained model toward export, serving and deployment.

items.title: Research
items.description: Use differentiation for scientific models and numerical experiments.

items.title: Systems
items.description: Explore profiling, distributed computation and accelerator operations.

lessons.title: A look inside the course.
lessons.intro: Read an explanation, make a prediction, then run and change the code. A few lessons from the journey:

items.summary: Prepare your workspace and run a first example.
Translate familiar NumPy operations into JAX.
Differentiate a function and check the result.
Apply one function across a batch of inputs.
Compile a function and understand its first call.
Connect training and evaluation in a model workflow.

projects.title: Put the pieces together.
projects.intro: Start with these two projects, then explore the specialist projects as you progress.
projects.scope: Staged CPU practice with exercises and checks. Each project states its prerequisites.

items.title: Audit a regression experiment
items.description: Fit a small model, check its gradients, and make the experiment reproducible.
items.alt: A linear model fits a line through observations, then its gradient is checked

items.title: Build a neural classifier
items.description: Connect a network, an optimizer, and an evaluation step. Investigate what happens when training goes wrong.
items.alt: Inputs pass through a hidden layer to a classifier output

offline.title: Take the course with you.
offline.intro: Read away from the browser. Keep the explanations beside your editor, or start with the first lesson online.
